design-system/src/components/_internal/S.why: NOT A DEFECT — the check's blind spot 1. The header's ground is set by child modifiers (&--created is --color-success, &--updated --color-info, &--cancelled --color-warning), which this reads as the page. White on those three is 6.17 / 4.53 / 3.52:1; the last is the same --color-warning question recorded below, in a place that is genuinely white-on-gold.

design-system/src/components/forms-and-i.why: LIVE, MARGINAL — 4.46:1 against primary's own 8% wash, a hair under 4.5. Not a mistake in this file: --color-primary is 5.02:1 on the page and passes there, and it fails here only because the wash lightens the ground. The fix is a token decision (#268 — does --color-primary need a darker text sibling, which is what --color-primary-text at 7.78:1 already is), not a per-call-site edit.
LIVE, MARGINAL — 4.20:1. Same as the state-08 entry above and slightly worse, because a 12% wash lightens the ground further. Same #268 decision.

EXEMPT, BUT WORTH A LOOK — the UNSELECTED star. It is the track of the rating rather than the value, and WCAG 1.4.11 exempts inactive components; the selected stars carry the meaning. Recorded rather than dismissed because 1.62:1 is faint enough that the empty half of a 2-of-5 rating is nearly invisible, and whether that reads is a design call.

design-system/src/components/layout-and-.why: NOT MEASURABLE HERE — the ground is `linear-gradient(transparent, var(--color-scrim))` over a photograph. The check composites the scrim over the page and gets 2.81:1, which is neither the top of the gradient nor the real image beneath. A caption over an arbitrary photo needs a scrim strong enough for the worst image, and only rendering can answer that.

design-system/src/components/status-and-.why: OPEN DECISION, ALREADY RECORDED — 3.7:1, the same pair in docs/evals/button-contrast-baseline.json. Does --color-warning need a darker filled variant, or --color-on-warning a darker on-colour? That is #268 and Bill's. Two checks reaching the same fact from different directions is the system working; it is one decision, not two.
